newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to hold general and regional poll March 1998.
newsitem.headline: France to hold general and regional poll March 1998.

text.p: The French government on Tuesday dropped plans to modify the regional voting system and said elections to regional councils would be held simultaneously with parliamentary elections scheduled in March 1998.

A statement from Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office said he abandoned plans to modify the regional polls system because political parties could not agree on a reform and he did not want to change the rules of the game so close to the election.

Juppe recently discussed with political leaders across the spectrum the date for the regional election, and plans to make it easier to find stable majorities in the 22 regional assemblies by reforming the strict proportional representation voting system.

Proportional representation gave anti-immigration crusader Jean-Marie Le Pen's far-right National Front the balance of power in some parts of the country in the last regional elections in 1992, forcing centre-right or left-wing coalitions to run minority executives with problems adopting a budget.
Maintaining the system will favour the Front, which has been kept out of the National Assembly by the first-past-the-post system used in national polls.
Juppe's Gaullist party last year rejected his suggestion to add a "dose" of proportional representation to the majority voting system for parliamentary elections.
Such a reform would likely open the National Assembly to the National Front. Le Pen won 15 percent of the vote in the 1995 presidential election.
